encounters.cc: Follow-up appointment for hypertension and diabetes mellitus. Patient expresses anger regarding a 45-minute wait time before being brought to the examination room.

lines: Follow-up appointment for hypertension and diabetes mellitus.
Patient expresses anger regarding a 45-minute wait time before being brought to the examination room.

The patient returns for follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, last evaluated in the Internal Medicine clinic on January 15, 2020, with subsequent interim follow-up for HIV infection in the Infectious Disease clinic on March 15, 2020.
He arrived on time but waited approximately 45 minutes before being brought to the examination room.

When the physician enters, the patient appears visibly angry and states, "You made me wait almost an hour! This is unacceptable." He crosses his arms, maintains eye contact, and appears otherwise calm and cooperative.
He does not refuse care or make threats but appears frustrated.
- Human immunodeficiency virus infection with history of AIDS (CD4 <200)
- Cystoscopy with bilateral ureteral stent placement (2019)
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/Emtricitabine 300 mg/200 mg PO daily
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Construction site foreman.
The physician intends to proceed with the encounter but wants to address the patient's frustration appropriately.

lines: Two-day history of increasing pain, redness, and swelling over the anterior aspect of the right knee after kneeling on gravel at a construction work site.
This 44-year-old male with HIV/AIDS and CKD and prior renal colic presents with a 2-day history of increasing pain, redness, and swelling over the anterior aspect of his right knee.
He denies any recent trauma but recalls kneeling on gravel and small stones at a work site last week.
- Human immunodeficiency virus infection with history of AIDS (CD4 <200)
- Cystoscopy with bilateral ureteral stent placement (2019)
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/Emtricitabine 300 mg/200 mg PO daily
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Construction site foreman.
On examination, the right knee is warm and erythematous with a fluctuant swelling over the prepatellar area.
The range of motion is limited due to pain.
Aspiration of the bursal fluid yields 50,000 WBC/µL with 90% neutrophils.
Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters.

encounters.cc: Two-week history of recurrent spontaneous nosebleeds with associated bruising on arms and legs, bleeding gums when brushing teeth, and prolonged bleeding from minor cuts.

lines: Two-week history of recurrent spontaneous nosebleeds with associated bruising on arms and legs, bleeding gums when brushing teeth, and prolonged bleeding from minor cuts.
The patient with stage 4 chronic kidney disease and HIV presents with bleeding symptoms following prior acute kidney injury and nephrolithiasis.
He states that he has also noticed bruises on his arms and legs without any remembered trauma.
Over the past few days, he reports bleeding from his gums when brushing his teeth and minor cuts taking unusually long to stop bleeding.
He reports significant fatigue but attributes it to poor sleep.
- Prerenal acute kidney injury secondary to hypovolemia (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Human immunodeficiency virus infection with history of AIDS (CD4 <200)
His medical history includes long-standing hypertension and poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.
He was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease 3 years ago and has not yet initiated dialysis.
- Cystoscopy with bilateral ureteral stent placement (2019)
He denies taking aspirin, NSAIDs, or anticoagulant medications.
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/Emtricitabine 300 mg/200 mg PO daily
He has no personal or family history of bleeding or clotting disorders.
He does not drink alcohol, smoke, or use illicit drugs.
Vital signs are within normal limits except for elevated blood pressure.
On physical examination, he has dried blood in his nares, scattered petechiae on both lower extremities, and ecchymoses on his forearms.
Cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations are unremarkable.
Neurological exam shows no focal deficits.
Laboratory studies reveal markedly elevated BUN and creatinine, consistent with advanced uremia.
He is admitted to the hospital for further evaluation.

encounters.cc: One-week history of fatigue and persistent bleeding from gums, with dark purple bruises on arms and thighs and prolonged bleeding from minor shaving cuts.

lines: One-week history of fatigue and persistent bleeding from gums, with dark purple bruises on arms and thighs and prolonged bleeding from minor shaving cuts.
The patient is a 46-year-old male with Stage 4 chronic kidney disease, HIV infection, and a prior bleeding presentation in July 2022 who returns with recurrent mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms.
He reports that brushing his teeth has become difficult due to frequent gum bleeding, and he also noticed that a small shaving cut bled for several hours before finally clotting.
Over the last few days, he has developed dark purple bruises on his arms and thighs, despite no significant trauma.
He denies use of aspirin, anticoagulants, or herbal supplements.
He has not had any recent infections or invasive procedures.
- Prerenal acute kidney injury secondary to hypovolemia (diagnosed 2021-07-15)
- Human immunodeficiency virus infection with history of AIDS (CD4 <200)
His medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
He was told several months ago that he may need dialysis soon, but he has not yet started it.
- Cystoscopy with bilateral ureteral stent placement (2019)
- Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/Emtricitabine 300 mg/200 mg PO daily
He is not sexually active and denies alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drug use.
Vital signs are within normal limits.
Physical exam reveals multiple ecchymoses on the upper and lower extremities, dried blood at the gumline, and bilateral lower extremity petechiae.
Cardiopulmonary and neurologic exams are unremarkable.
His platelet count, PT, and aPTT are all within the normal range.
Renal panel shows markedly elevated BUN and creatinine consistent with longstanding renal failure.
